.²1 <ab>N.</ab> of Indra.
.²2 <ab>N.</ab> of a king of the Vidyādharas, hero of the play called Nāgānanda;
 (mentioned also in {#kaTAsaritsAgara#}). [He was the son of Jīmūtaketu
 and renowned for his benevolent and charitable disposition. When his fatherʼs
 kingdom was invaded by his kinsmen, he scorned the idea of fighting with
 them and induced his father to leave it to those who sought for it and
 to repair with him to the Malaya mountain to lead a holy life. It is related
 that there he one day took the place of a young serpent who was, by virtue
 of an agreement, to be offered to Garuḍa as his daily meal, and induced,
 by his generous and touching behaviour, the enemy of serpents to give
 up his practice of devouring them. The story is very pathetically told in the play].
